action: Farmers and USDA partners: expect intermittent outages of USDA payment and status tools; use official USDA channels for updates and verify any unexpected USDA email or call before sharing information.
date_note: Date is the Nextgov report; the internal disclosure was earlier that week (an email sent Monday).
exec: A US federal agency that pays farmers has taken applications offline after a security incident; the cause and any data loss are not yet known.
plain: The US Department of Agriculture has had a security incident, and staff took several systems offline, including tools used to pay farmers. It is not yet clear who did it or whether any data was taken.
summary: Nextgov reports, citing three anonymous people and an internal email and bulletin it viewed, that USDA applications were taken offline over several days after a security incident disclosed internally this week. The email says database passwords were reset in all environments. Affected tools include financial systems for payments to farmers. Nextgov says it is unclear who was responsible or whether data was taken; USDA has not commented publicly.
title: USDA takes multiple systems offline after internal security incident

validation.note: Single publisher (Nextgov/FCW, with Government Executive also viewing the documents) relying on anonymous sources and internal notices; no on-record USDA statement.

review.note: Compared title, summary, date and single_source status against the Nextgov/FCW article: anonymous sources, Monday internal email, database passwords reset in all environments, farmer payment tools offline, cause and data theft unknown, no USDA comment. No actor named, severity 2 fits.
